insert into public.meal (slug,name,planned_date,status,pax,workflow_md,shared_prep_md,wine_pairing) values ($m$dry-aged-pork-tomahawk-dinner$m$,$m$Dry-Aged Pork Tomahawk Dinner$m$,$m$2026-09-27$m$,$m$cooked$m$::meal_status,3,$m$*Sunday 27 September 2026 · Serves 3 · Target service 6:00 pm, floating 5:45–6:15 · Restrained French bistro register* ## Menu - Reverse-seared dry-aged Gooralie pork tomahawk, with crisp-rind belly and crackling - Sharp cider–shallot jus - Potato purée - Shaved fennel and Granny Smith salad - Charred hispi cabbage ## Critical path Loin pull at 130°F / 54°C → 8-min rest → sear → rest and safety check → carve → serve. Service floats with the loin's exit from the oven (E+0); everything after exit is keyed to E. ## Failure prioritization Do not delay the loin's rest, sear or safety check for anything. The purée absorbs timing drift (loosen with warm milk). The jus rewarms and the salad waits undressed. If the belly rind has not puffed by E+18, serve the loin and send the belly after. The crackling is optional and can be dropped. ## Oven sequencing The oven holds 225°F / 107°C for the loins, belly pieces and finished crackling; there are no temperature changes. At E+0, switch the oven off, crack the door for 1 min, then put the plates in to warm; the crackling stays in with them. ## Heat allocation and parallel work
Heat sourceJob
OvenLoins and belly low roast from 4:45; crackling hold; plate warming after E+0
Induction 1Jus build (2:30–3:20); rewarm from E+0
Induction 2Purée (4:40–5:20); contingency reheat at E+10
TigerPurée hold from 5:20 (planned max 60 min, designed)
BinchotanLit 4:55; loin sear only, from E+8
Outdoor gas burner 1Hispi, from E+3
Outdoor gas burner 3Crackling 4:00–4:25 (optional); belly crisping from E+0
**Runs in parallel after E+0:** the loin rest, belly crisping, hispi and jus rewarm. The sear (E+8) cannot overlap the carve or the jus finish; both wait for the loin. ## T-minus timeline — before the loin leaves the oven (nominal service 6:00)
TimeAction
Sat (done)Belly split from the loins; rind taken off the loin fat caps; belly cut into ~8 cm pieces, rind into ~3 cm strips. Belly + rind (631 g) salted with 5 g, rind-up, uncovered overnight. Loins unsalted, loosely covered.
T-255 (1:45)Weigh the loins; salt at 0.8%. Refrigerate uncovered on a rack (3-hr brine).
T-210 (2:30)Build the jus (~50 min).
T-150 (3:30)Jus strained, cooled in a shallow container, refrigerated.
T-120 (4:00)Optional: crisp the rind strips on burner 3 (15–25 min). Pour the rendered fat into a bowl for the belly.
T-105 (4:15)Preheat the oven to 225°F / 107°C. Pork goes in once the oven reads temperature.
T-80 (4:40)Purée potatoes on (~40 min to Tiger).
T-75 (4:45)Loins and belly pieces in, fridge-cold; crackling on the same rack. Probe in the loin eye, alarm 127°F / 53°C.
T-65 (4:55)Light the binchotan (ready by 5:25; holds for hours). Quarter and season the hispi.
T-55 (5:05)Shave the fennel and shallot, make the dressing; chill undressed.
T-40 (5:20)Purée into the Tiger on Keep Warm (ceiling 6:20; contingency trigger 6:00).
5:25–5:55Exit window. Pull the loin at 130°F / 54°C = E+0. Record total oven time.
## After the loin leaves the oven (E+)
TimeAction
E+0Loin onto a rack, uncovered, probe still in — 8-min rest. Oven off, plates in (crackling stays in). Jus on very low. Belly rind-down in the reserved fat on burner 3 (12–18 min).
E+3Hispi on burner 1 (9–14 min).
E+8Reading #2, remove probe. Sear per the reading-#2 gate (4–6 min). Reading #3 at the stop; record contact time.
E+10Cut the apple, dress the salad (hold ≤10 min).
E+12–18Hispi and belly finish; hold both uncovered.
E+14Loin rests uncovered on a rack (≥4 min).
E+15Check the purée; loosen with warm milk 10 ml at a time if tight.
E+16Jus off heat; whisk in 15 g cold butter.
E+18Reading #4 (≥145°F / 63°C) + plate temperature. Carve. Adjust the jus against an end slice.
E+20Plate: purée, hispi, loin, belly and crackling beside, jus around the loin, salad last. Serve.
*If the plating window slips, the loin crust and the belly rind soften first.* ## Arithmetic check - **Earliest exit 5:25 (serve 5:45):** purée hold 25 min; loin brine 3 hr; hispi hold 3–8 min; belly hold 2–8 min. Passes. - **Latest exit 5:55 (serve 6:15):** purée hold 55 min (within 60); binchotan lit 68 min at the sear (burns for hours). Passes. - **Beyond the band:** if the loin is still in the oven at the trigger (20 min before the Tiger ceiling — 6:00), the purée leaves the Tiger, is covered, and is reheated on induction 2 at E+10. The 60-min hold is never extended. ## Holding chain
ComponentHoldMax holdDriftCorrective
JusRefrigerated; rewarmed on very lowRewarm ≤20 minTightensThin with unsalted stock
PuréeTiger Keep Warm60 min (designed)StiffensWarm milk, 10 ml at a time
CracklingRack in the 225°F oven, then the switched-off ovenUntil plating (designed)Softens in humidity1 min rind-down in the belly pan
SaladChilled undressed; dressed E+10Dressed ≤10 minWiltsDrain; serve
HispiUncovered, warm10 minSoftensNone; serve
BellyUncovered on a rack10 minRind softensKeep away from the jus
LoinUncovered rackPrescribed rests only——
## Meal balance Richness comes from the loin fat, the belly, the crackling and the purée. Acid does three distinct jobs: cider vinegar gives the jus depth and edge, lemon gives the salad a palate reset, and a little lemon may correct the hispi. Sweetness from the apple family (medium-dry cider, Granny Smith) is controlled by a tart apple and the full vinegar reserve. Temperature runs from hot pork and hispi, through warm purée, to the cold salad. Texture: crust, crackling and crisp rind, silky purée, raw crunch, charred leaf. No chilli. ## To confirm after the cook The 130°F / 54°C pull and four-point series; the reading-#2 sear thresholds; the 40–70 min oven band at 3.5 cm; the belly rind-down crisp (12–18 min) after an overnight dry salt; the crackling method and oven hold; the 60-min Tiger hold; the hispi timings.$m$,$m$

### Sourcing notes - One lemon covers both the salad and the hispi. - Cider: Thatchers Gold is medium dry, not brut, so expect to use all 4 ml of the reserved cider vinegar at the finish. - Potatoes: Russet, Agria or Maris Piper. Purchase weight allows for peeling; the recipe runs on peeled weight. - No hispi: Savoy (quarters, same timings), round green cabbage (eighths; rounded side 4–6 min), or tenderstem broccoli (5–7 min, start at E+10).$m$,null);

update public.dish set method_md=$m$## Dish Overview Deep binchotan crust over juicy, faintly pink loin with the dry-aged character leading; crisp-rind belly and crackling alongside. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: 2 loins with bone, belly pieces and crackling; serves 3 · Active: ~40 min · Loin brine: 3 hr same-day; belly: overnight · Low roast: 40–70 min (designed) · Oven: 225°F / 107°C · Leave-in probe in the oven only; Thermapen at the fire* ## Prep Phase **1. Saturday (done):** belly split from each loin along the outer face of the rib, bone left with the loin; rind sliced off the loin fat caps leaving ~5 mm fat. Belly in ~8 cm pieces, rind in ~3 cm strips; 631 g salted with 5 g, rind-up, uncovered overnight on a rack. The butcher's scoring is kept as is — no re-scoring. **2. 1:45 — loins:** weigh, salt all surfaces at 0.8%, refrigerate uncovered on a rack for 3 hr. ## Active Cooking ### Crackling (optional, 4:00) **3.** Rind strips into cold cast iron on outdoor burner 3. Render over medium-low, then raise the heat until the skin blisters. Stop on sight and sound: blistered, glassy skin, fat rendered out — no temperature target (15–25 min, designed). **4.** Pour the rendered fat into a heatproof bowl for the belly. Hold the crackling on a rack; it goes into the oven with the pork at 4:45. ### Loin and belly **5.** Preheat the oven to 225°F / 107°C at 4:15. At 4:45, once it reads temperature, pat the loins and belly dry and set them on a rack over a tray, fridge-cold, with the crackling alongside. **6.** Insert the leave-in probe sideways into the centre of a loin eye, clear of bone and fat seams. Set the alarm at 127°F / 53°C. **7. Pull the loins at 130°F / 54°C (E+0, reading #1).** Expected finish 145–150°F / 63–66°C; rise +15 to +20°F (designed, not validated). Record total oven time. The belly comes out at the same time. **8.** Rest the loins uncovered on a clean rack with the probe still in, 8 min. At E+8, log reading #2 and remove the probe before the binchotan. **9. Reading #2 gate (designed thresholds):** below 136°F / 58°C — normal colour-led sear with fat-edge stand; 136–139°F / 58–59°C — sear hard, minimal time between faces, fat-edge stand ≤60 s; 140°F / 60°C or above — maximum heat, shortest sear giving full colour, no fat-edge stand. **10.** Pat dry, film lightly with the oil (oil the meat, not the grate) and add the pepper. Sear over the hottest binchotan zone in 60–90 s passes per face, plus the fat-edge stand as the gate allows. Stop on colour: deep mahogany across both faces. Record contact time. Thermapen the centre (reading #3). **11. Belly, from E+0:** cast iron on burner 3 over medium with the reserved fat, rind-down, pressed flat under a heavy pan for the first 3–4 min; use a splatter guard. Stop when the rind is blistered, puffed and glassy-crisp, then give the other faces 1–2 min to colour (12–18 min, designed). Thermapen the meat to ≥145°F / 63°C; hold on a rack. ## Holding & Assembly **12.** Rest the loins uncovered on a rack, ≥4 min, so the crust does not steam. **13. E+18, reading #4 (Thermapen) plus plate temperature.** Safety floor: ≥145°F / 63°C with a 3-min rest — the safety requirement, separate from the culinary target. **14.** Carve the loin off the bone, across the grain, 8–10 mm / ⅓–⅜ in thick. Slice the belly across into 1.5–2 cm pieces and set them rind-up beside the loin with the crackling. Jus around the loin, never over the crust, belly or crackling. ## Critical Control Points
ClassFailure ModeSensory CueRecovery
MajorLoin below the safety floorReading #4 under 145°F / 63°CBinchotan edge 60 s per side, rest 3 min, recheck
MajorMissed pullProbe past 135°F / 57°C at exitOne colour-only pass. Above 150°F finish: unrecoverable for juiciness; serve extra jus
MajorGrey crustNo mahogany after the first passPat dry, hottest zone, second short pass
MajorBelly rind not puffedRind still flat and leathery at E+18Serve the loin; 2–3 more min over higher heat and send the belly after
MinorCrackling stays leatheryNo blistering after 25 minRaise the heat 5 min; if still leathery, drop it (optional component)
## Adjustment Notes Salt is weight-controlled — do not season carved slices; add jus instead. If the plate reads too rich, correct the acid in the jus, not on the meat. ## Cook Log

*#2 − #1 = pre-sear drift · #3 − #2 = sear gain · #4 − #3 = carryover.*$m$, summary=coalesce(nullif(summary,''),$m$Dry-aged Gooralie pork tomahawk loins salt-brined at 0.8%, low-roasted at 225°F / 107°C to a 130°F / 54°C pull, rested and seared over binchotan to a mahogany crust, served with crisp-rind belly pieces and optional crackling rendered from the loin rind.$m$), servings=coalesce(servings,3), equipment=case when coalesce(array_length(equipment,1),0)=0 then array[$m$oven$m$,$m$rack over a tray$m$,$m$leave-in probe thermometer$m$,$m$Thermapen$m$,$m$binchotan grill$m$,$m$cast iron pan$m$,$m$outdoor gas burner$m$,$m$heavy pan (for pressing belly)$m$,$m$splatter guard$m$,$m$heatproof bowl$m$,$m$ruler$m$,$m$kitchen scale$m$]::text[] else equipment end, designed_unvalidated=case when coalesce(jsonb_array_length(designed_unvalidated),0)=0 then $m$[{"param": "Pull temperature", "designed_value": "130°F / 54°C (alarm 127°F / 53°C)", "note": "Reading #1 at E+0; insert into public.dish (slug,name,protein,category,cuisine,difficulty,tags,occasion,status,source,governance_version,summary,method_md,servings,equipment,designed_unvalidated,nutrition_estimate) values ($m$tomahawk-cider-shallot-jus$m$,$m$Sharp Cider–Shallot Jus$m$,null,array[$m$Sauce$m$]::text[],array[$m$French$m$]::text[],$m$Medium$m$,array[$m$jus$m$,$m$cider$m$,$m$shallot$m$,$m$reduction$m$,$m$make-ahead$m$,$m$pork$m$]::text[],array[$m$Sunday dinner$m$]::text[],$m$cooked$m$::dish_status,$m$Recovered from dry-aged-pork-tomahawk-dinner.docx, generated 27 September 2026$m$,null,$m$Lean, glossy pan-independent jus: shallots sweated in butter, medium-dry cider reduced to ~80 ml with thyme, then unsalted chicken stock and staged cider vinegar reduced to ~220 ml, chilled and finished at service with cold butter and the reserved vinegar.$m$,$m$## Dish Overview A lean, glossy jus built independently of the roasting tray: cider for depth, cider vinegar staged for edge. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: ~220 ml / 7½ fl oz · Total: ~50 min · Active: ~20 min · Made at 2:30, chilled, rewarmed at E+0* ## Prep Phase **1.** Measure the cider and stock separately. Set aside the reserved 4 ml vinegar — it is not used until service. ## Active Cooking **2.** Sweat the shallots in 10 g butter with a pinch of salt over medium-low, 6–8 min. Stop when translucent, without colour. **3.** Add the cider and thyme over medium-high. Reduce to ~80 ml / ⅓ cup, until the raw alcohol smell has gone (10–15 min). **4.** Add the stock and 4 ml vinegar. Reduce over medium-high to ~220 ml. Stop when it lightly coats a spoon. **5.** Strain. Cool in a shallow container and refrigerate by 3:30. ## Holding & Assembly **6.** E+0: rewarm over very low heat until steaming. Do not boil. **7.** E+16: off heat, whisk in the 15 g cold butter. **8.** E+18: once the loin is carved, taste against an end slice. The medium-dry cider means you will likely need all of the reserved vinegar: add it 1 ml / ¼ tsp at a time, then salt and pepper. ## Critical Control Points
ClassFailure ModeSensory CueRecovery
MajorOver-reducedSyrupy or sticky; heavy coat on the spoonThin with unsalted stock, 15 ml / 1 tbsp at a time
MajorReads sweetSweet rather than savoury-sharp against the porkReserved vinegar in steps; do not mask with salt
## Adjustment Notes Too sharp — whisk in 5–10 g cold butter. Too salty — dilute with unsalted stock.$m$,3,array[$m$induction hob$m$,$m$saucepan$m$,$m$fine strainer$m$,$m$shallow container$m$,$m$whisk$m$,$m$spoon$m$]::text[],$m$[{"param": "Rewarm hold", "designed_value": "≤20 min on very low", "note": "Holding chain: tightens; thin with unsalted stock."}, {"param": "Reserved vinegar at finish", "designed_value": "4 ml held; expect to use all of it", "note": "Because Thatchers Gold is medium dry, not brut; add 1 ml at a time."}]$m$::jsonb,null);

insert into public.dish (slug,name,protein,category,cuisine,difficulty,tags,occasion,status,source,governance_version,summary,method_md,servings,equipment,designed_unvalidated,nutrition_estimate) values ($m$tomahawk-potato-puree$m$,$m$Potato Purée$m$,null,array[$m$Side$m$]::text[],array[$m$French$m$]::text[],$m$Easy$m$,array[$m$potato$m$,$m$purée$m$,$m$mash$m$,$m$Tiger hold$m$,$m$make-ahead$m$]::text[],array[$m$Sunday dinner$m$]::text[],$m$cooked$m$::dish_status,$m$Recovered from dry-aged-pork-tomahawk-dinner.docx, generated 27 September 2026$m$,null,$m$Silky neutral purée of floury potatoes boiled from cold salted water, dried in the pan, riced hot and folded with warm milk and butter in three additions, held in the Tiger on Keep Warm for up to 60 min.$m$,$m$## Dish Overview Silky, neutral potato purée; the crust, crackling, raw fennel and charred hispi supply the contrast. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: modest adult portions, larger portion for Lukas · Total: ~40 min · Active: ~20 min · Tiger Keep Warm from 5:20* ## Prep Phase **1.** Peel and cut the potatoes; keep them under cold water until cooking. ## Active Cooking **2.** 4:40: cover with cold water by 2–3 cm, add the salt, bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-low. Stop when a knife passes through the centre with no resistance (15–20 min). **3.** Drain well. Return to the hot pan over low heat for 1–2 min, shaking, until the steam visibly drops. **4.** Rice while hot. Warm the milk and butter together until the butter melts, without boiling. Fold in over three additions; stop as soon as it is smooth. ## Holding & Assembly **5.** 5:20: into the Tiger on Keep Warm.
